youtube.title: Why Your Ears Pop On A Plane ✈️ #Shorts #science #facts #didyouknow
youtube.description:
Your ears pop on a plane because of a tiny tube most people have never heard of.

Air behind your eardrum must match the cabin pressure. As it changes on climb and descent, the eardrum bulges until the Eustachian tube, linking ear and throat, opens. Swallowing, yawning or chewing opens it: pop.

Watch our full episodes on the channel.
